subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the public API be a nested `ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork`/per-agent policy instead of the requested top-level `allowPrivateNetwork` key?
rationale: The source shows the implementation primitive exists, but exposing it changes the SSRF boundary and the current maintainer discussion rejects the first top-level shape without deciding the final public contract.

options.title: Adopt nested audited policy
options.body: Land a nested `web_fetch` SSRF policy, ideally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming, audit warnings, docs, cache separation, and redirect/metadata tests.

options.title: Add only a global broad opt-in
options.body: Expose a simpler global private-network toggle, accepting the larger blast radius and documenting that operators own the risk.

options.title: Reject broad private access
options.body: Keep arbitrary `web_fetch` strict and direct users to trusted proxies, narrow fake-IP flags, or separate tools for internal services.

recommendation.title: Adopt nested audited policy
recommendation.body: Land a nested `web_fetch` SSRF policy, ideally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming, audit warnings, docs, cache separation, and redirect/metadata tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible combination of SSRF/web_fetch history and prior maintainer-context review on the rejected top-level shape.
